$comment: A/B for cp_admm_scale_free -- the L3 lexicographic cascade solved in a non-dimensional frame, with the r-ridge relative to each CP's own ||c_i||^2 and the minimum-usage point of the optimal face selected.

Motivation: rho, inner_abs_tol and both ADMM residuals are absolute constants carrying MW, while r is dimensionless and the coupling constraint sigma + sum_i r_i c_i <= B - theta is homogeneous, so the optimal r is invariant under rescaling the data but the solver is not. On simbench_lv_* the CPs are ~3.6 kW (||c_i||^2 ~ 1.4e-5) and every residual is under admm_abs_tol=1e-3 at the end of the FIRST iteration of each tier -- before the r-update has seen the tier's binding constraint through z/u. The cascade returns its r=0 initialisation with converged=True. Measured offline on a traced gas_dependent round: iterations=4 (four tiers x one iteration), gas coverage -0.00%; the same problem scaled 10x gives 217%. With the flag on, r is identical to 12 digits across six decades of scaling and lands at 100.0% of the sector deficit in ~60-170 iterations, degrading gracefully to ~124% at the gossip path's ~10 iterations/round.

This supersedes the earlier r_regularization hypothesis: alpha cancels at the fixed point when minimize_usage is off, so it only sizes the FIRST r-step -- which is what gated the stopping test. Holding alpha at 0.1 and moving inner_abs_tol 1e-3 -> 1e-4 alone flips coverage 0% -> 218%.
Arms: default (flag on) vs the legacy counterfactual, crossed with the two solver paths so gossip and the replicated kernel are both covered.

Judge on: cp_generation_breakdown / CP dispatch being non-zero on the two dependent grids, gas and heat PWSF, and that electricity PWSF and slack compliance do not regress -- electricity is the CPs' INPUT sector, so a fleet that finally dispatches draws real power.
name: ab_cp_admm_scale_free
